title: Stateful sources: a counter and a round-robin cycle

blocks.text: A `Supplier` takes nothing and returns a value, and every `get()` runs its lambda again, so a supplier that keeps state can hand out a different value on each call. `IntSupplier` does the same with `int getAsInt()`, and no boxing.

items: `counter(int start, int step)` returns an `IntSupplier` that yields `start`, `start + step`, `start + 2*step`, …
`cycling(List<T> items)` returns a `Supplier<T>` that yields the items in order and starts over after the last.

blocks.text: A program may hold several sources at once. An empty list has nothing to cycle through: throw `IllegalArgumentException("items must not be empty")`. Watch what the supplier captures: a `List` the caller still holds is a mutable object.

cases.says: Each getAsInt returns the next number, starting at start and moving by step.
Each get returns the next item, going back to the first after the last.
Two sources made by the same method do not share a position.
An empty list is rejected when the cycle is created, not later on get.
The cycle captures a copy, so changing the caller's list afterwards does not change it.

concepts: Each get() runs the lambda again, so a Supplier with state can return a new value on every call.
IntSupplier returns a primitive int through getAsInt, with no boxing.
A Supplier that captures a mutable object sees every later change made to it.
